points: The woman bare a son and called his name Samson, and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Samson saw a woman of the Philistines in Timnath and told his parents, get her for me to wife. They asked, is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren? He answered, get her for me, for she pleaseth me well. Purely visual reasoning, like the brother who sees nothing he likes in his congregation and grabs one online or in another city, hoping she will understand all this later.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Samson insisted, get her for me, for she pleaseth me well. The forefathers always charged their sons not to do this.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: As Samson went down to the vineyards of Timnath, a young lion roared against him, challenging him. Here you begin to see the divine power on Samson.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: He went down and talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: His father went down unto the woman, and Samson made there a feast, as the young men used to do, and when the Philistines saw him they brought thirty companions to be with him.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: Samson put forth a riddle: if they could declare it within the seven days of the feast, he would give them thirty sheets and thirty change of garments, and if they could not, they would give him the same.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: On the seventh day they said unto Samson's wife, entice thy husband that he may declare unto us the riddle, lest we burn thee and thy father's house with fire. They threatened to burn their own countrywoman in her father's house over thirty outfits.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: His anger was kindled, and he went up to his father's house, and Samson's wife was given to his companion, whom he had used as his friend; she was his wife to be, for they had not yet consummated the marriage.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: Within a while, in the time of wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a kid and said, I will go in to my wife into the chamber. He knew she had betrayed him and still went back to her; a weakness for a woman really does beat on Israelite men.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: Samson said concerning them, now shall I be more blameless than the Philistines, though I do them a displeasure; he was set to avenge himself.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes by himself, took firebrands, turned the foxes tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst between two tails.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: The Philistines asked who had done this, and were told, Samson, the son in law of the Timnite, because he had taken his wife and given her to his companion.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: Samson said unto them, though ye have done this, yet will I be avenged of you, and after that I will cease; he would get the last word.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: The Philistines went up and pitched in Judah and spread themselves in Lehi, and the men of Judah asked, why are ye come up against us? We are already under tribute; what is the problem? They answered, to bind Samson are we come up, to do to him as he hath done to us. Samson was not even of Judah; he was a Danite.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: Three thousand men of Judah went to the top of the rock Etam and said to Samson, knowest thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us? what is this that thou hast done unto us? Instead of standing with their brother, the whole tribe came to hand him over to the oppressor.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: Samson said, with the jawbone of an ass, heaps upon heaps, with the jaw of an ass have I slain a thousand men.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: Samson went to Gaza, the chief city of the Philistines, and saw there an harlot and went in unto her; once again the whoremongering spirit had hold of this brother.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: It was told the Gazites that Samson was come, and they compassed him in and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, quiet all the night, saying, in the morning, when it is day, we shall kill him.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: Samson lay till midnight, arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all, upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron. They wanted to wait at the gate for him, so he took the gates.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth. Why do you need to know that? That is a setup. He was so gone he was not even paying attention to it.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

points: Delilah asked Samson outright, tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee. She was literally asking him for the formula to get him killed.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: He told her, if they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak and be as another man. The lords of the Philistines brought them up, she bound him, with liers in wait abiding in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: Delilah took new ropes and bound him, with liers in wait in the chamber, and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he brake them from off his arms like a thread.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: She pressed the third time, and he told her, if thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web. She fastened it with the pin and said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; he awaked out of his sleep and went away with the pin of the beam and with the web.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: She said, the Philistines be upon thee, Samson; and he awoke out of his sleep and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the Lord was departed from him. He thought he was going into beast mode like before, but it was over, because he had broken his vow; the hair was shaved from off his head.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, an idolatrous ritual, and to rejoice, for they said, our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.

They gave the praise and the glory to their idol, a devil that had not done a thing. Really it was Samson's own transgression that caused the Most High to allow the Philistines to bind and afflict him; that praise to a fake god did not please the Most High.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: When their hearts were merry, they said, call for Samson, that he may make us sport; and they called for him out of the prison house and set him between the pillars, using the Israelite man for entertainment and mockery while they honoured their idol.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them: the two main pillars that bore up the whole building, one at his right hand and one at his left.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: Now the house was full of men and women, all the lords of the Philistines were there, and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women that beheld while Samson made sport.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: Samson called unto the Lord and said, O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life. Remember Judges 14:4: the Lord sought an occasion against the Philistines, and even with Samson's failings and flaws the Most High used him as a vessel of vengeance on the heathen who oppressed his people and gave the glory of their victory to a fake god.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

cases.preview: A Nazarite to God from the womb, with a lust for heathen women that is the infamy his story is known for.
